meta.title: AIXTRON SE — Felix Grawert's MOCVD compound-semiconductor deposition franchise through the GaN power, SiC, and micro-LED cycles
meta.abstract: AIXTRON SE (Frankfurt Xetra: AIXA; SDAX index member) is the principal German metal-organic chemical vapor deposition (MOCVD) equipment supplier — its tools deposit the compound-semiconductor epitaxial layers (GaN, SiC, GaAs, InP) that go into power electronics, micro-LED displays, laser diodes, photonics, and RF devices. Headquartered in Herzogenrath near Aachen, Germany. Strategic narrative through 2024-2026 has centered on the GaN power electronics inflection (GaN-on-Si for automotive, data-center and consumer power), the SiC power equipment cycle, the still-uncertain micro-LED display thesis, and CEO Felix Grawert's leadership through the post-Schulte transition.

chapters.title: Snapshot
chapters.body:
## AIXTRON at a Glance

Four decades after its founding ~~as a spin-off from RWTH Aachen University and the Max Planck Institute~~ ==in 1983 by employees of the Institute for Semiconductor Technology at RWTH Aachen==, AIXTRON SE had reinvented its revenue mix once already — surviving the LED MOCVD supercycle and its violent unwind — and ~~by 2025 stood positioned for a second structural inflection, this time driven by compound semiconductors in power electronics~~ ==by the May 2026 snapshot stood positioned for another demand inflection, this time led by optoelectronics demand for AI data-centre photonics==. The company trades on Frankfurt Xetra as AIXA.DE, a member of the ~~SDAX~~ ==MDAX and TecDAX==, and is headquartered in Herzogenrath in the Aachen region, a few kilometres from its academic birthplace. Felix Grawert, ~~President of the Executive Board and sole CEO since Bernd Schulte's retirement at the end of 2023~~ ==Chairman of the Executive Board, CEO & President since March 2021 after joining the Executive Board in August 2017==, had built the equipment franchise around two platform generations — the G5 and the G10 — and by 2025 was pivoting its commercial narrative toward AI infrastructure as the next durable demand vector.

## Fiscal 2025 in Brief

Full-year 2025 revenue came in at [€556.6 million](https://compoundsemiconductor.net/article/123615/Aixtron_posts_robust_results_in_a_tough_market) (approximately $615 million at prevailing rates), a 12% contraction from the €633.2 million recorded in 2024. Order intake declined more gently, to €544.3 million from €596.4 million, leaving an equipment backlog of €257.8 million at year-end. EBIT fell to €100.3 million, compressing the operating margin from 21% to 18% — a result that arrived at ~~the top~~ ==the midpoint== of the company's revised full-year guidance range of 17–19%, and well above the analyst fears that had stalked the stock through mid-year.

| Metric | FY2024 | FY2025 | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| Revenue | €633.2m | €556.6m | −12% |
| Order intake | €596.4m | €544.3m | −9% |
| EBIT | €131.2m | €100.3m | −24% |
| EBIT margin | ~21% | 18% | −3 pp |
| Gross margin | ~41% | 40% | −1 pp |
| Free cash flow | ~~Negative~~ ==−€72.4m== | €181.9m | — |

The 18% EBIT margin masked a more meaningful shift in product mix. Power electronics — combining GaN and SiC tools — accounted for 57% of system revenue in 2025, with optoelectronics at 23% and LED/micro-LED at 15%. A year earlier, micro-LED and conventional LED had together represented 28% of the mix. The compression was direct: Apple's cancellation of its smartwatch micro-LED programme, reported in early 2024, rippled through AIXTRON's order book and pulled the segment's revenue share nearly in half.

## The Platform Architecture

AIXTRON's revenue is built around two distinct MOCVD tool families. The G10-GaN platform serves the gallium nitride power electronics market — GaN-on-Si and GaN-on-SiC epitaxy for devices used in data centre power supplies, EV onboard chargers, and consumer adapters. Customers include Infineon, Navitas Semiconductor, Power Integrations, Innoscience, and GaN Systems. AIXTRON holds an estimated 71% share of the global GaN MOCVD equipment market, a structural dominance that reflects its first-mover depth in the process chemistry.

The G10-SiC platform is younger and occupies more contested ground. SiC CVD epitaxy for power devices pits AIXTRON against ASM International (which acquired LPE to strengthen its SiC position), Veeco (which purchased Swedish start-up Epiluvac in a deliberate move to enter the market), and a cluster of Chinese domestic equipment makers receiving state backing. AIXTRON's share in SiC CVD is estimated at 33–37%, and the company's stated differentiation centres on the 150mm-to-200mm wafer transition — a process window where it argues the G10-SiC platform offers superior defect density control. ~~By H1 2025, AIXTRON had delivered its 100th G10-SiC system~~ ==In Q3 2025, AIXTRON reported shipment of its 100th G10-SiC system==, a volume milestone that signalled commercial traction even as Western SiC end-market demand softened.

The third platform revenue stream — optoelectronics — was effectively dormant as a growth driver through most of 2025 before igniting sharply. The G10-AsP system, which deposits GaAs and InP epitaxy for laser diodes, DFB lasers, and VCSELs, had established itself as the tool of record at leading laser manufacturers by mid-year. Customers such as II-VI/Coherent, Lumentum, Sumitomo Electric, and Mitsubishi Electric draw on the platform for datacom lasers feeding AI data centre optical interconnects.

## The 2026 Inflection

A first-quarter 2026 order surge changed the tenor of the company's year. Q1 2026 order intake reached €171 million — up roughly 30% year-on-year — with optoelectronics comprising more than 65% of that figure. AIXTRON raised its full-year 2026 revenue guidance in April from an initial €520 million (±€30 million) to €560 million (±€30 million), and lifted the EBIT margin range to 17–20%.

> "The significantly stronger-than-expected demand from the Optoelectronics sector in the first quarter is a very encouraging development... With our G10-AsP system, we have the tool of record for the next generation of photonic components." — Felix Grawert, April 2026

GaN power, by contrast, was described as ~~"stable but soft"~~ ==stable to moderate== in Q1 2026, while SiC was characterised as "weak" owing to substantial global overcapacity built by Wolfspeed, STMicroelectronics, and Chinese producers over the prior two years. Yet Grawert's forward framing was explicit:

> "We expect that AI data centers can become the largest single application for GaN power semiconductors in the near future."

## What the Dossier Asks

The forward research questions that animate this dossier are tightly bounded. How durable ~~is the GaN power inflection~~ ==could a prospective GaN power inflection be== once AI data centre power-delivery architectures shift toward 48V and higher-density rack designs? Can AIXTRON defend or expand its SiC CVD share against ASM/LPE and Veeco as the 200mm transition compresses incumbent advantages? What is the residual value — and timeline — of the micro-LED display thesis now that the Apple Watch programme has lapsed and early-stage AR device orders remain sporadic? How does German two-tier governance — Vorstand under Grawert, Aufsichtsrat above — constrain or enable capital allocation at a company ~~carrying €273 million in net cash by end of Q1 2026~~ ==with €272.7 million of cash and current financial assets at March 31, 2026 and a €450 million zero-coupon convertible bond placed in April 2026==? And how does a EUR-reporting, globally-selling equipment company manage the translation exposure as dollar-denominated tool orders reprice against euro manufacturing costs? These are the questions the chapters that follow will attempt to answer.

chapters.title: From 1983 RWTH Aachen spin-off through LED cycles to GaN power and SiC inflection
chapters.body:
## Aachen's Compound-Semiconductor Laboratory, 1983

The company that would become Europe's pre-eminent maker of compound-semiconductor deposition equipment began not in a boardroom but ~~in the laboratories of RWTH Aachen University and the adjacent research networks of the Max Planck Gesellschaft~~ ==with employees of the Institute for Semiconductor Technology at RWTH Aachen University==. When ~~researchers there spun out~~ ==they founded== a dedicated metal-organic chemical vapour deposition business in 1983, the commercial logic was modest: universities and advanced device laboratories needed reactor equipment capable of growing III-V semiconductor crystals with atomic-layer precision, and the Aachen group had developed that capability. The founding name reflected its origins — AIX, a shorthand for Aachen's chemical-vapour heritage, appended to the suffix TRON to signal industrial ambition.

Herzogenrath, a small city on the German–Dutch border straddling the Wurm river, became the permanent home of AIXTRON SE's manufacturing and engineering base. The proximity to RWTH Aachen sustained an enduring pipeline of graduate engineers and a collaborative relationship with academic researchers that the company would cite in investor materials for decades. Unlike the Silicon Valley model of clean breaks from institutional predecessors, AIXTRON carried the Aachen academic culture forward into its engineering DNA — a tendency toward methodical incremental improvement of reactor geometry and gas-flow dynamics rather than disruptive platform leaps.

Through the 1980s and into the early 1990s, the business served a niche: research institutes, defence-linked compound-semiconductor fabs, and early optoelectronic device manufacturers buying systems capable of growing gallium arsenide, indium phosphide, and related III-V materials. Revenue was measured in tens of millions of euros and the customer roster was small. The key technological advance of those years was the multi-wafer planetary reactor concept, which allowed simultaneous epitaxial growth across multiple wafers by rotating each wafer around its own axis on a gas-cushion bearing — a design that would underpin every subsequent product generation.

## The LED Decade and Its Aftermath

The transformational event for AIXTRON came from an unexpected direction. As solid-state lighting and consumer displays drove adoption of gallium nitride LEDs through the 2000s, the demand for MOCVD reactors capable of growing GaN on sapphire substrates exploded. Asian device manufacturers — initially in Taiwan, Japan, and South Korea, then in rapidly expanding volume in mainland China — needed precisely the multi-wafer planetary reactors that AIXTRON had spent two decades refining. The company's AIX 2000 and successor systems became standard equipment in LED chip fabs across the region.

Between roughly 2007 and 2012, AIXTRON's revenues scaled sharply, reaching ~~a peak of approximately €700 million in the fiscal year 2011~~ ==€783.8 million in fiscal 2010 before declining to €611.0 million in fiscal 2011== as Chinese LED manufacturers, backed by provincial government subsidies and aggressive capacity targets, placed equipment orders at a pace the industry had never seen. For a company headquartered in a small German city and employing fewer than two thousand people, the growth was dizzying.

The correction was equally severe. By 2012 and 2013, Chinese LED fabs had built far more capacity than the nascent solid-state lighting market could absorb. New orders collapsed, utilisation rates at customer facilities fell sharply, and AIXTRON's order intake entered a multi-year trough. Revenue declined toward the €150–€200 million range and the company posted losses. The LED boom had made AIXTRON; the LED bust exposed an uncomfortable concentration risk in a single application and a single geography.

The episode left marks on how subsequent management would think about portfolio construction. The dependence on Chinese LED volume customers — firms whose buying behaviour was driven as much by subsidy cycles and local government directives as by genuine equipment demand — proved difficult to forecast and impossible to hedge. A company whose core technology was broadly applicable to multiple compound-semiconductor applications had allowed itself to be defined, for a critical window, almost entirely by one of them.

The vulnerability became acute in 2016 when a consortium led by Fujian Grand Chip Investment Fund, a Chinese state-linked vehicle, proposed an acquisition of AIXTRON. The German federal government ~~intervoked its foreign investment review powers and ultimately withdrew the clearance it had initially granted, blocking the transaction~~ ==withdrew and reopened the clearance it had initially granted, while the offer lapsed after the U.S. national-security review and presidential order prevented a closing condition from being met==. The episode accelerated a broader German and European reckoning with technology-sector acquisitions by state-linked foreign buyers, and it left AIXTRON operating as an independent company at a moment when it needed a strategic reset.

## Grawert and the Strategic Rebuild, 2017–2023

Felix Grawert arrived at AIXTRON in 2017 ~~from McKinsey, where he had advised technology and industrial clients, and was appointed to the Executive Board~~ ==after serving at Infineon Technologies from 2013 to 2017, and joined the Executive Board in August 2017== — initially sharing leadership with Bernd Schulte, the company's long-serving chief executive and co-architect of its LED-era growth. The pairing placed a strategically-oriented ~~outsider~~ ==semiconductor executive== alongside an engineer-executive who had built the operational and manufacturing platform over many years. Grawert was ~~confirmed as President of the Executive Board and Chief Executive Officer in 2018~~ ==appointed Chairman of the Executive Board, Chief Executive Officer and President in March 2021==, formally leading the strategic reorientation that had begun to take shape.

The pivot had a clear logic. GaN-on-silicon and GaN-on-SiC power electronics were entering a commercialisation phase after years of laboratory development. The physical properties of gallium nitride — higher breakdown voltage, faster switching speed, and lower on-resistance than silicon — made it attractive for power conversion applications in electric-vehicle onboard chargers, data-centre power supply units, and high-efficiency consumer adapters. SiC power devices served an overlapping but distinct segment, with particular strength in high-voltage traction inverters for electric vehicles and grid-connected power systems. Both application areas required MOCVD epitaxial growth equipment. AIXTRON already had the reactor design competence; the question was whether the commercial markets would develop on a timescale relevant to the company's planning horizon.

The product platform that emerged from this period was the G10 series — a family of large-format multi-wafer planetary reactors optimised for GaN-on-silicon and, subsequently, SiC epitaxy. The G10-GaN and G10-SiC tools represented a deliberate move up the performance and pricing curve, targeting production-scale fabs building capacity for power electronics rather than the lower-margin research and LED markets. The parallel G5 platform continued to serve GaAs, InP, and speciality compound-semiconductor applications including laser diodes for datacom transceivers, VCSELs for 3D-sensing modules, and automotive LiDAR sources.

Schulte, who had anchored AIXTRON's continuity through the LED peak, the trough, and the blocked acquisition, ~~retired from the Executive Board at the end of 2023 after a tenure measured in decades~~ ==left the Executive Board in 2021 after a tenure measured in decades==. His departure closed one era and left Grawert as the company's sole executive face — a concentration of strategic authority that the company's German two-tier governance structure, with its Aufsichtsrat supervisory board providing oversight, was designed to accommodate.

## The GaN Power and SiC Inflection, 2023–2025

The years between 2023 and 2025 validated, at least partially, the strategic thesis that Grawert had been constructing since his arrival. G10-GaN system shipments scaled as device manufacturers — ranging from Infineon and STMicroelectronics in Europe to Wolfspeed and Navitas in North America and Innoscience in China — invested in GaN-on-silicon epitaxial capacity. The adoption curve in consumer power adapters, driven by the proliferation of USB Power Delivery and gallium nitride charger designs from brands including Anker and Belkin, had produced a tangible volume pull-through that justified production-scale reactor investment.

Data-centre power conversion added a structurally larger demand vector. The accelerating buildout of AI compute infrastructure placed unprecedented demand on power delivery efficiency, and GaN-based power factor correction and conversion designs offered meaningful efficiency gains that hyperscale operators translated directly into operating-cost reductions at the data-centre level. By the time AIXTRON reported its fiscal 2024 results, revenue had recovered to ~~a range above €600 million — a level that returned the company near its 2011 LED-era peak~~ ==€633.2 million, slightly above fiscal 2023 revenue of €629.9 million and below the fiscal 2010 LED-era peak== but on a far more diversified application base and with meaningfully higher average selling prices per system.

SiC entered the revenue mix more slowly, reflecting the longer qualification cycles and the entrenched position of existing SiC epitaxy suppliers in a market that Wolfspeed and others had structured around proprietary process relationships. The G10-SiC platform was commercialised and shipped, but its contribution to total order intake through 2024 remained modest relative to GaN.

The one application that had been expected to contribute materially — and did not — was micro-LED display. The thesis had posited that AIXTRON's MOCVD equipment would be required in volume for the epitaxial growth steps underpinning next-generation micro-LED displays for consumer electronics. Reports emerged in early 2024 that Apple had postponed or cancelled its micro-LED programme for the Apple Watch, a development that removed what had been the most credible near-term demand signal from the display application pipeline. The micro-LED thesis was not abandoned — the physics of micro-LED displays still required compound-semiconductor epitaxy — but its contribution to AIXTRON's planning horizon receded into a longer-dated, more speculative position, leaving ~~GaN power and SiC as the principal growth levers entering 2025 and beyond~~ ==GaN power, SiC and a later optoelectronics rebound as the principal growth levers entering 2025 and beyond==.

chapters.title: G10-GaN, G10-SiC, photonics MOCVD, broader compound-semi equipment
chapters.body:
## The G10 Platform: AIXTRON's Power Electronics Engine

The G10-GaN reactor sits at the centre of AIXTRON's commercial renaissance in power electronics. Developed as a successor to the G5 platform that had served the LED era, the G10 was optimised for 200-millimetre gallium-nitride-on-silicon production — the substrate combination that made GaN power devices economical enough for automotive and data-centre applications at volume. Where the G5 had been a workhorse of LED epitaxy, the G10 ~~repackaged AIXTRON's close-coupled showerhead reactor architecture~~ ==extended AIXTRON's Planetary Reactor architecture into a high-throughput 150/200-millimetre GaN platform== for the specific demands of power-device epi: tighter thickness uniformity, precise aluminium-gallium-nitride barrier control, and the thermal management necessary for thick GaN buffers grown atop large-diameter silicon wafers.

The commercial case for the tool converged with a structural shift in power conversion. Automotive on-board chargers migrating from silicon IGBTs to GaN transistors, data-centre rack power-supply units targeting 97-per-cent conversion efficiency, and the proliferation of 100-watt-plus USB-C fast-charger adapters all created simultaneous demand for GaN epitaxial wafers at a scale that strained the industry's installed deposition capacity. Customers including Innoscience — whose fabs in China were among the most aggressive GaN-on-Si capacity build-outs through 2023 and 2024 — alongside Navitas Semiconductor, Infineon Technologies, and STMicroelectronics were all competing for G10-GaN reactor delivery slots during the 2022–2024 build cycle.

Felix Grawert, addressing investors during AIXTRON's 2023 results presentation, characterised the dynamic in terms of structural adoption rather than cyclical demand:

> "We are seeing genuine technology adoption here — GaN is replacing silicon in power conversion applications where the efficiency and power-density benefits are unambiguous. This is not a single customer or a single geography. It is broad-based."

That breadth was visible in order-intake geography. Chinese GaN power device makers, spurred by government-backed semiconductor self-sufficiency programmes, represented a meaningful share of G10-GaN order flow through 2023 and into 2024. The concentration introduced customer-mix risk, but it also validated the platform's positioning as the reference tool for a nascent production ecosystem.

## G10-SiC: Staking a Claim Against CVD Incumbents

The G10-SiC programme represented a deliberate stretch into territory historically dominated by hot-wall chemical vapour deposition equipment suppliers — a different MOCVD-adjacent market where AIXTRON's reactor expertise offered a differentiated entry point rather than incumbency.

Silicon carbide epitaxy for power devices — the growth of thin n- and p-type SiC layers on bulk SiC substrates — had long been served by high-temperature CVD tools from suppliers including LPE and Nuflare, operating at temperatures above 1,500 degrees Celsius in horizontal hot-wall reactors. AIXTRON's proposition with the G10-SiC was that a planetary-reactor MOCVD approach, leveraging the company's accumulated understanding of gas-phase uniformity and rotating-disc hydrodynamics, could deliver competitive epi quality at throughputs and defect levels suited for automotive-grade SiC MOSFETs.

The commercial stakes were substantial. Wolfspeed, STMicroelectronics, Infineon, and a cohort of Chinese SiC makers including SICC and TankeBlue were all constructing SiC epitaxy capacity ahead of anticipated electric-vehicle drivetrain demand in the 2025–2028 window. Even a modest share of the SiC epi-tool market — considerably larger in aggregate capital expenditure than the GaN power segment — would represent a material revenue diversification for a company whose revenue base was ~~roughly EUR 600 million in 2024~~ ==EUR 633.2 million in FY2024==.

Grawert was measured about the SiC timeline in public communications, acknowledging that displacing established hot-wall CVD tools in a conservative, automotive-qualified supply chain required demonstrating defect density and run-to-run repeatability at production scale, not just in application laboratories. The G10-SiC entered early customer qualification cycles during 2023 and 2024, with commercial shipments tracking behind the GaN platform's ramp but accumulating process data that management described as encouraging.

| Platform | Substrate | Primary End Markets | Competitive Landscape | Status (as of 2024) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| G10-GaN | GaN-on-Si, GaN-on-SiC | Auto OBC, data centre PSU, fast charge | ~~Veeco EPIK 868~~ ==Veeco Propel / Propel Power GaN MOCVD==, in-house epi | Commercial ramp |
| G10-SiC | SiC-on-SiC | EV drivetrain inverters, industrial | LPE, Nuflare hot-wall CVD | Early qualification |
| ~~G5+ photonics~~ ==G10-AsP / G5+ photonics== | GaAs, InP | Datacom lasers, VCSELs, LiDAR | Veeco K475i, ~~Thomas Swan~~ ==in-house epi== | Mature/stable |

## Photonics MOCVD: The Quiet Annuity

While the G10 power platforms attracted the bulk of investor attention, AIXTRON's photonics MOCVD franchise continued to generate steady equipment orders and aftermarket revenue from a geographically diversified customer base that had been constructing datacom and sensing capacity with ~~G5-series tools for more than a decade~~ ==legacy G5-series tools and AIXTRON's Planetary Reactor-based G10-AsP platform in current high-volume GaAs/InP deployments==.

The photonics segment spans three primary application clusters. Datacom transceivers — the edge-emitting laser diodes and electroabsorption-modulated lasers that carry 400G and 800G optical traffic inside hyperscale data centres — are grown on gallium arsenide and indium phosphide substrates in AIXTRON reactors operated by fabs aligned with II-VI/Coherent, Lumentum, and Sumitomo Electric. Automotive LiDAR brought a second demand vector: pulsed 905-nanometre edge-emitting lasers for time-of-flight ranging systems, where AIXTRON's GaAs epi tools were already qualified in the supply chains of Tier-1 automotive laser suppliers. VCSELs for consumer 3D sensing — the structured-light modules behind smartphone face-unlock and gesture-recognition systems — constituted a third, more volatile stream sensitive to platform upgrade cycles at handset OEMs.

The photonics book was not a growth story in the 2022–2025 period; it was a durability story. Datacom laser capacity builds tracked data-centre construction with a lag, and the VCSEL market oscillated with consumer electronics cycles. But the installed base of AIXTRON photonics reactors in customer fabs — each requiring periodic process-kit replacement, spare-part provisioning, and calibration services — generated recurring aftermarket revenue with margins structurally above the equipment sale. AIXTRON's services and spare-parts line, consolidated within its aftermarket reporting, provided a partial hedge against the lumpiness of new-tool orders across all product lines.

## Micro-LED: The Thesis Under Stress

No segment illustrated the asymmetry between thesis and execution more sharply than micro-LED display epitaxy. Through 2021 and 2022, AIXTRON had articulated a credible case for MOCVD demand expansion driven by micro-LED display adoption: the technology required high-brightness InGaN or AlInGaP epitaxy at wafer scale, and AIXTRON's planetary reactors were the natural supply point for a display ecosystem that was in active development at Apple, Samsung Display, and several Asian panel makers.

The thesis carried sufficient credibility that analysts incorporated micro-LED option value into sum-of-the-parts valuations of AIXTRON through 2023. Then, in early 2024, press reports — subsequently corroborated by supply-chain sources — indicated that Apple had cancelled or substantially deferred its Apple Watch micro-LED programme, citing yield and cost challenges in mass transfer and display module assembly that were outside AIXTRON's control but that removed the anchor customer whose adoption curve the broader display industry had been watching.

The cancellation exposed how much of the micro-LED equipment investment case had rested on a single flagship programme providing proof-of-volume. Without an Apple Watch series launch to validate micro-LED at consumer price points, display panel makers retrenched their pilot-scale capacity orders. AIXTRON retained some micro-LED activity — university research tools, specialty display development at Samsung and a handful of Chinese display developers, and continued process-development engagements — but the multi-hundred-million-euro capacity wave that bulls had anticipated for 2024 and 2025 did not materialise within the frozen snapshot window.

Grawert acknowledged the deceleration without abandoning the long-term thesis. The segment, he noted, remained technically compelling; the question was timing, not direction. The practical consequence for AIXTRON's medium-term revenue profile was ~~a more concentrated dependence on power electronics — GaN power and, progressively, SiC — to sustain the revenue base that had been partially underwritten by micro-LED expectations~~ ==a more uneven mix: optoelectronics carried the main near-term demand impulse by the April 2026 update, while GaN power was stable to moderate and SiC power was weak amid industry overcapacity==.

## Aftermarket, Services, and the Recurring Revenue Layer

Across all tool families, AIXTRON's aftermarket and services business provided ballast against the capital-equipment cycle. The installed base of G5 and G10 reactors in customer fabs required a steady flow of process kits — susceptors, liners, inlet components — that degraded with use and required periodic replacement to maintain epi quality. Extended service agreements, remote diagnostics, and process-optimisation consulting added revenue streams that were structurally less volatile than equipment orders.

AIXTRON did not provide granular aftermarket-revenue disclosure in the format common among US-listed equipment peers such as Applied Materials or Lam Research, but management commentary through 2023 and 2024 indicated that services and spares represented a meaningful and growing share of total revenue as the installed GaN power base expanded. Each G10-GaN tool shipped to a customer fab represented a years-long service relationship; at the volume of G10 deployments accumulated through the 2022–2024 ramp, the compounding annuity of process-kit consumption was becoming a non-trivial revenue contributor that partially smoothed the lumpy new-equipment order book.

The aggregate picture by the frozen snapshot date in May 2026 was of a company whose product architecture had been substantially repositioned — from LED MOCVD toward ~~GaN power, SiC power, and photonics~~ ==optoelectronics/photonics, GaN power, and SiC power== — with micro-LED as a residual optionality rather than a near-term volume driver. The G10-GaN platform had achieved commercial scale; ~~the G10-SiC was in qualification~~ ==the G10-SiC platform had reached the 100th-system shipment milestone reported in Q3 2025==; ~~photonics tools were a stable annuity~~ ==optoelectronics/photonics tools were both a stable installed-base annuity and the main near-term demand driver==; and micro-LED remained the chapter whose conclusion the industry had not yet written.

chapters.title: Revenue trajectory, order intake cyclicality, EBIT margin progression, capital allocation
chapters.body:
The four fiscal years from 2022 through 2025 trace the full arc of a compound-semiconductor capital-equipment cycle: the demand surge that carried AIXTRON from mid-tier profitability to ~~its best-ever results~~ ==the strongest results of its recent GaN/SiC investment cycle==, the plateau, and the controlled compression that followed as GaN power adoption paused and micro-LED display orders failed to materialise. Read in sequence, the numbers form a precise record of both the franchise's earnings power and the structural risks that attend a concentrated, capital-equipment business model exposed to the idiosyncratic buildout timelines of a handful of device chipmakers.

## The Revenue Surge and Its Arithmetic

The fiscal-year pivot came in 2023. After posting revenue of €463.2m in FY2022—itself a respectable 8 per cent gain over the prior year—AIXTRON booked €629.9m in FY2023, a 36 per cent step-change that ranked as the company's strongest annual revenue growth in more than a decade. The catalyst was multifaceted: volume shipments from the G10-GaN platform ramp gathered pace as Infineon, STMicroelectronics, Navitas Semiconductor, and Chinese power-device fabs accelerated GaN-on-Si and GaN-on-SiC capacity expansion; the SiC power epitaxy tool portfolio contributed an incremental stream of orders from Wolfspeed and European tier-one device makers; and optoelectronics deliveries—laser-diode and VCSEL tools for datacom and 3D-sensing—maintained a steady underlying contribution. Felix Grawert, addressing analysts in the February 2024 earnings call, characterised the outcome with characteristic precision:

> "We have successfully continued our growth trajectory and expect strong further growth for 2025 and continuation of our growth trajectory with a further significant growth in revenues."

FY2024 came in almost exactly flat at €633.2m—an increase of less than 1 per cent—revealing that the surge had run its initial course. Revenue plateaued as a handful of large customers digested equipment already received, even as the next wave of demand orders began to rebuild. The picture for FY2025 was more difficult: revenue contracted 12 per cent to €556.6m, the largest single-year decline since the post-LED-bubble correction of 2012–2013, as soft GaN power orders in Asia combined with USD headwinds and the absence of any material micro-LED display business to produce a year in which AIXTRON outperformed only on the cash line.

| Fiscal Year | Revenue (€m) | YoY Change | EBIT (€m) | EBIT Margin |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| FY2022 | 463.2 | +8% | 104.7 | 22.6% |
| FY2023 | 629.9 | +36% | 156.8 | 24.9% |
| FY2024 | 633.2 | +1% | 131.2 | 20.7% |
| FY2025 | 556.6 | −12% | 100.3 | 18.0% |

*Sources: [AIXTRON Annual Report 2023](https://www.aixtron.com/en/investors); [AIXTRON FY2024 results press release](https://www.finanzwire.com/press-release/aixtron-well-on-track-in-a-challenging-market-environment-UgcGf0OTr0e); [AIXTRON FY2025 results press release](https://www.webdisclosure.com/press-release/aixtron-se-etr-aixa-aixtron-with-robust-results-in-a-soft-market-environment-yyvmiE66gVE)*

## Order Intake Cyclicality and Backlog Dynamics

For a company whose revenues are delivered with a lag of six to eighteen months after booking, order intake and equipment backlog are the forward-facing vital signs. The FY2022 order intake of €585.9m—18 per cent above the prior year and the second-highest annual figure in AIXTRON's history at the time—seeded the FY2023 revenue surge. The FY2023 order intake of €640.7m, a further 9 per cent gain, signalled that FY2024 revenue would hold: it did, exactly. The deceleration that began in the second half of 2023 then manifested in the order line with a one-cycle lag. FY2024 order intake fell 7 per cent to €596.4m; FY2025 declined a further 9 per cent to €544.3m. Equipment order backlog—the unconverted portion of booked orders—peaked at €353.7m at the end of FY2023 and had eroded to €257.8m by end-FY2025, a 27 per cent drawdown over two years.

| Fiscal Year | Order Intake (€m) | Equipment Backlog (€m) |
|---|---|---|
| FY2022 | 585.9 | 351.8 |
| FY2023 | 640.7 | 353.7 |
| FY2024 | 596.4 | 289.3 |
| FY2025 | 544.3 | 257.8 |

The composition of the order book shifted substantially during this period. Asia—principally China—contributed a disproportionate share of the FY2022–FY2023 surge as domestic GaN power-device fabs (Innoscience, GaN Systems affiliates, and multiple unnamed entrants) competed to scale capacity. By 2024 that Chinese ordering wave had largely exhausted its first-cycle appetite, and European and South Korean customers were not yet sufficient to replace the volume. Q4 2024 order intake of €157.0m fell 23 per cent against the same period a year earlier; Q4 2025's partial recovery to €169.6m, up 8 per cent, provided the first concrete inflection signal since the downturn began.

## EBIT Margin Progression and Management's Implicit Targets

AIXTRON's EBIT margin trajectory across the four-year window illustrates the leverage—both positive and negative—inherent in a business with high operating costs and relatively sticky R&D expenditure. At the FY2022 EBIT margin of 22.6 per cent, the company already exceeded its publicly communicated guidance band of 20–23 per cent. The FY2023 result of 24.9 per cent sat at the lower end of a mid-year-upgraded guidance range of 25–27 per cent, reflecting a mix effect as volume pulled ahead of realised product-margin improvement. Management has not published a formally labelled "mid-cycle" or "through-cycle" EBIT margin target in the manner of, say, an industrial conglomerate issuing a Capital Markets Day framework; the closest functional equivalent is the 25 per cent level demonstrated in FY2023, which analysts and investors have treated as the proxy peak-cycle target.

The FY2024 compression from 24.9 to 20.7 per cent was caused by three concurrent pressures: unfavourable product mix as a higher proportion of revenue derived from lower-margin repeat orders rather than new-platform tool sales; a step-up in R&D expenditure to €91.4m (14.4 per cent of revenue) as the next-generation Hyperion 300mm GaN platform advanced toward commercialisation; and the first meaningful FX headwind as the US dollar softened relative to the euro. FY2024 initial guidance had targeted 24–26 per cent; the actual outcome of 20.7 per cent represented a significant miss. In the FY2024 results call, CFO Dr. Christian Danninger acknowledged that 2025 would be focused on "strengthening profitability and rebuilding a strong cash position."

The FY2025 EBIT margin of 18.0 per cent, landing at the midpoint of a final revised guidance range of 17–19 per cent, represented the lowest margin since the pre-GaN-power era. Grawert was characteristically measured about the near-term context:

> "In 2025 AIXTRON has performed well in a challenging market environment. We efficiently adjusted our capacity and significantly increased our free cash flow by over EUR 250 million."

The 2026 guidance issued in February 2026—subsequently raised in April 2026 to 17–20 per cent EBIT margin on revenue guidance of ~~€560–620m~~ ==around €560m, plus or minus €30m==—signalled that management regarded FY2025 as a trough rather than a reset, with the optoelectronics cycle, particularly AI-driven datacom laser tools, positioned as the primary recovery driver.

## R&D Intensity and the Investment Cycle

One of the more instructive features of the FY2022–FY2025 data is the deliberate decision to maintain, and indeed accelerate, research and development expenditure through the revenue downturn. R&D climbed from €57.7m in FY2022 (12.5 per cent of revenue) to €91.4m in FY2024 (14.4 per cent), before stepping back slightly to €81.1m in FY2025 (14.6 per cent on the lower revenue base). The FY2024 R&D peak coincided with simultaneous development programmes across the G10 tool family completion, early-stage Hyperion platform engineering, and SiC tool qualification work. This cycle of investment-before-revenue is structurally embedded in AIXTRON's model: platform transitions—from G5 to G10, from 150mm to 200mm substrate compatibility, from 200mm to 300mm GaN—require multi-year R&D commitments before any tool sale materialises. The consequence for the margin line is an unavoidable earnings dilution during transition periods that a shorter-cycle business would not exhibit.

## Dividends, Buybacks, and Cash Allocation

The dividend history across the four years traces an arc that closely mirrors the net-income trajectory, with one sharp episode of policy recalibration. AIXTRON paid €0.31 per share for FY2022 and raised that to €0.40 for FY2023, the highest absolute dividend in the company's modern history and a clear signal that management believed the earnings upgrade was durable. The abruptness of the reversal made an impression: the FY2024 dividend was cut to €0.15 per share—a 62.5 per cent reduction—directly reflecting the net profit decline from approximately €145m in FY2023 to €106.2m in FY2024. The FY2025 dividend was held at €0.15, consistent with a roughly 17–20 per cent payout ratio on FY2025 net income of €85.3m. The payout ratio has therefore normalised to a conservative level, prioritising balance-sheet liquidity over shareholder distribution at a moment when the investment cycle for Hyperion and for the €40m Malaysia manufacturing facility (production readiness targeted for mid-2027) competes for capital allocation.

No active share buyback programme was in operation during FY2022–FY2024. ~~At the May 2025 Annual General Meeting, shareholders authorised management to repurchase and cancel treasury shares~~ ==The pre-2026 repurchase authority dated to the May 25, 2022 Annual General Meeting, and the May 13, 2026 Annual General Meeting approved a replacement authorization before the snapshot date==, but no specific programme size or execution timeline had been disclosed by the frozen snapshot date of 23 May 2026. The authorisation exists as an option, not a commitment.

## Free Cash Flow and Balance Sheet Reconstruction

The free cash flow record over the period tells a more volatile story than the income statement alone suggests. FY2022 produced a modest free cash flow of €7.7m despite strong profitability, as the working capital cycle absorbed the order-intake surge in advance inventory. FY2023's €629.9m revenue year generated negative free cash flow of €109.7m—an apparent paradox explained by a combination of heavy CapEx associated with the Aachen innovation centre expansion and a substantial build in finished-goods inventory as production ramped ahead of deliveries. FY2024 produced a further negative €72.4m in free cash flow, compressing ~~cash and equivalents~~ ==cash and cash equivalents plus other current financial assets== to €64.6m at year-end, AIXTRON's lowest liquid-asset balance in the cycle. The FY2025 reversal was dramatic: operating cash flow of €208.4m and free cash flow of €181.9m rebuilt the ~~cash line~~ ==cash and current-financial-assets line== to €224.6m by year-end, a €160m recovery driven by inventory drawdown, disciplined CapEx restraint, and the structural back-loading of customer prepayments into the second half of the year. ==By 31 March 2026, cash and current financial assets had risen further to €272.7m, and the April 2026 placement of a €450m zero-coupon convertible bond added a material new financing instrument to the snapshot-date balance-sheet context.==

## FX Translation and the EUR/USD Sensitivity

AIXTRON reports in euros but generates a material portion of revenue in US dollars from Asian customers and through USD-denominated contracts. The company typically communicates an annual budget exchange-rate assumption in its guidance: FY2024 was budgeted at 1.15 USD/EUR; FY2025 initial guidance assumed 1.10 (implying a stronger dollar). When the actual rate drifted toward 1.15 during 2025, management flagged in the October 2025 guidance revision that the FX shift alone accounted for approximately one percentage point of the gross-margin reduction and one percentage point of the EBIT-margin reduction in the full-year result. The FY2026 budget rate of 1.20 USD/EUR—reflecting a weaker dollar assumption relative to the FY2025 starting point—embeds another potential headwind. As a structural matter, a sustained move from 1.10 to 1.20 compresses AIXTRON's reported EBIT margin by roughly one percentage point on a through-cycle basis, all else equal, with no operating offset available absent renegotiation of USD contracts or further euro-zone cost reduction. The FX exposure is asymmetric in its P&L impact: revenue translates lower in euro terms while the cost base—predominantly labour and procurement in Germany—remains largely euro-fixed.

chapters.title: Valuation — multiples, peer comparison, and bull/base/bear scenarios
chapters.body:
## A ~~De-rated~~==Re-rated== Franchise at a Cyclical Inflection

By the frozen snapshot of 23 May 2026, AIXTRON had ~~passed through one of the more dramatic multiple compressions in European capital-equipment history~~==completed a violent valuation round trip in European capital equipment==. The stock that briefly touched the high-€30s during the 2022–2023 compound-semiconductor euphoria — when every analyst spoke of the GaN power revolution as if it were already delivered — ~~was trading in the low-to-mid teens by early 2025 and had not fully recovered to that territory by the close of the dossier window~~==had rebounded to about €53.68 on 22 May 2026, the last trading day before the frozen snapshot==. ~~Investors who bought the story at peak had endured roughly a 60 percent drawdown from the cycle high, a punishment comparable to what the LED MOCVD boom inflicted a decade earlier.~~==Investors who bought at the euphoric high still endured a severe interim drawdown; by the dossier close AIXTRON was valued above that earlier share-price peak, so the valuation question had shifted to whether earnings and cash flow could catch up.==

The precise market capitalisation at the frozen date ~~carries uncertainty: AIXTRON's last disclosed share count was approximately 200 million shares, and recent traded prices on Frankfurt Xetra had oscillated in a range of roughly €13 to €17 over the preceding six months~~==is anchored by the last trading day before the frozen snapshot: AIXTRON's Dec. 31, 2025 share-capital baseline was 113,456,120 issued shares, and AIXA traded around €53.68 on 22 May 2026==. ~~At the midpoint of that band — call it €15 per share — the implied market capitalisation was approximately €3.0 billion.~~==That implies equity market capitalisation of roughly €6.1 billion.== ~~AIXTRON carried a net cash position consistently above €300 million through 2024 (the company disclosed no material debt obligations), which would place enterprise value at roughly €2.6–2.7 billion.~~==Cash and current financial assets were €224.6 million at Dec. 31, 2025 and €272.7 million at Mar. 31, 2026, and the April 2026 zero-coupon convertible bond added €450 million of gross debt-like financing; using the Mar. 31 liquidity figure and the convertible, enterprise value was roughly €6.25–6.3 billion before any conversion-dilution treatment.== All multiples below are derived from that approximate EV baseline unless otherwise noted; readers should treat them as directional, ~~not decimal-precise, given the absence of a single confirmed closing price for 23 May 2026~~==not decimal-precise==.

## Current Multiples and What They Imply

Against ~~fiscal-2024 revenue described in the company's own disclosures as being in the €600-million-plus range~~==actual FY2025 revenue of €556.6 million, down 12 percent, and FY2026 guidance around €560 million, plus or minus €30 million==, EV/Sales works out to approximately ~~4.3–4.5x trailing~~==11.3x trailing and roughly 11x forward at the guidance midpoint==. That is ~~below~~==above== the 6–8x range AIXTRON commanded during the 2022–2023 re-rating when compound-semi enthusiasm was at its zenith, and it sits ~~closer to the trough multiples the stock carried during the 2019–2020 LED-MOCVD hangover~~==well beyond the trough multiples the stock carried during the 2019–2020 LED-MOCVD hangover==.

On earnings, AIXTRON historically targets EBIT margins in the 20–30 percent band in cycle-healthy years. ~~If 2024 delivered a mid-cycle EBIT margin of approximately 20–22 percent on €600 million of revenue, operating earnings would be in the €120–132 million range, with net income (at an effective tax rate near 25 percent) of roughly €90–99 million. That puts trailing P/E at approximately 30–33x — elevated by industrial standards but less egregious for a specialist franchise with demonstrated 30-percent EBIT ceilings in prior upcycles. Forward P/E, applying modest consensus growth into 2025, narrowed toward the low-to-mid 20s, closer to where the stock looked fairly valued on a sum-of-cycles basis.~~==The relevant snapshot baseline was FY2025 actual EBIT of €100.3 million at an 18 percent margin, the midpoint of the final 17–19 percent range, followed by Q1 2026 revenue of €59.4 million and FY2026 EBIT-margin guidance around 17–20 percent. At the FY2026 revenue-guidance midpoint, that implies operating earnings of roughly €95–112 million; after a 25 percent tax assumption, net income would be roughly €71–84 million. That puts forward P/E at roughly 72–86x on the corrected €6.1 billion equity value — a demanding multiple even for a specialist franchise with demonstrated high-margin upcycle economics.==

~~EV/EBITDA, adding back depreciation and amortisation of roughly €30–35 million annually, implied a trailing multiple in the 16–18x range. Price-to-book was harder to calculate precisely without the final 2024 balance sheet, but given AIXTRON's track record of generating equity through retained earnings — total equity had exceeded €700 million in prior filings — P/B appeared to sit somewhere near 4x, again below the 2022–2023 peak but above the company's pre-GaN baseline.~~==EV/EBITDA, adding back depreciation and amortisation of roughly €30–35 million annually to the FY2026 EBIT-guidance framework, implied a forward multiple in the low-to-high 40s. Price-to-book was harder to calculate precisely without rebuilding the full FY2025 equity bridge, but the corrected equity value put P/B materially above 4x and made the market's premium to retained earnings and balance-sheet optionality explicit.==

## Historical Multiple Compression: A Five-Year Arc

The re-rating from 2020 to 2023 was driven by two intersecting narratives: the GaN power electronics inflection, which genuinely had industrial substance; and the micro-LED display thesis, which did not. At the peak, AIXTRON carried forward P/E multiples above 35x and EV/Sales above 7x — valuations that implied a sustained-growth story more typical of a fabless semiconductor company than a capital-equipment cyclical. The subsequent de-rating was sharp and, on reflection, predictable. The Apple Watch micro-LED programme was reported as cancelled or indefinitely deferred in early 2024; Chinese customers, who had represented a meaningful share of order intake, faced export-control ambiguity; and the GaN power ramp, while real, proved lumpy rather than linear.

By late 2024 the stock had retraced nearly to its 2020 lows. ~~The partial recovery into the €13–17 range through early 2026 suggested investors were beginning to discount a normalised GaN power cycle without micro-LED optionality — a more conservative, arguably more honest, read of the underlying business.~~==The rebound to around €53.68 by 22 May 2026 suggested investors had moved from trough repair to a scarcity-and-reacceleration valuation. A conservative read of the underlying business became the downside case: optoelectronics strength, GaN normalisation, and any micro-LED optionality had to translate into sustained cash flow to support the price.==

## Peer-Group Comparison

AIXTRON's closest comparables span North American semi-equipment specialists and European deposition peers. The table below uses estimated multiples near the frozen date, drawing on public filings and market commentary; figures for peers are approximate and should be cross-referenced against each company's latest disclosures.

| Company | Ticker | EV/Sales (fwd) | EV/EBITDA (fwd) | P/E (fwd) | Principal overlap |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| AIXTRON | AIXA.DE | ~~4.3x~~==~11x== | ~~16x~~==~46x== | ~~23x~~==~78x== | GaN/SiC/micro-LED MOCVD |
| Veeco Instruments | VECO | ~2.5x | ~11x | ~18x | MOCVD, ALD; direct competitor |
| ASM International | ASMI.AS | ~7x | ~21x | ~30x | Deposition (ALD/Epi); European comps |
| Axcelis Technologies | ACLS | ~3.2x | ~12x | ~17x | Power semi ion implant; SiC exposure |
| Kulicke & Soffa | KLIC | ~2.8x | ~10x | ~18x | Advanced packaging; semi cyclical |
| Onto Innovation | ONTO | ~5x | ~18x | ~27x | Compound semi inspection; GaN/SiC |

Two observations stand out. First, AIXTRON commands a premium to direct MOCVD competitor Veeco across every metric — ~~a premium that is historically justified by AIXTRON's deeper installed base, superior margins, and more advanced GaN platform, but that narrows in bear scenarios if Veeco closes the technology gap in SiC epitaxy~~==a premium that requires AIXTRON to sustain a clear technology lead, convert the optoelectronics-led 2026 demand recovery into orders, and defend margins if Veeco narrows the gap in GaN or SiC epitaxy==. Second, ~~AIXTRON trades at a discount to ASM International, which carries a premium as a high-margin ALD franchise with structural AI-accelerated logic tailwinds. That gap arguably reflects both the cyclicality discount embedded in compound-semi equipment and the residual micro-LED overhang still weighing on AIXTRON's narrative.~~==AIXTRON trades at a premium to ASM International on the corrected headline multiples, even though ASM carries the cleaner high-margin ALD franchise and structural AI-accelerated logic tailwinds. That inversion places the burden of proof on AIXTRON's 2026–2028 earnings step-up rather than on simple mean reversion from a depressed multiple.==

## Intrinsic-Value Framing: What Cash-Flow Trajectory the Price Implies

A simplified DCF using the approximate ~~€2.65 billion EV~~==€6.25–6.3 billion EV== and a terminal-growth rate of 3 percent (consistent with long-run semiconductor equipment market growth) required a sustainable free-cash-flow level of roughly ~~€160–180 million per year~~==€375–440 million per year== to justify current pricing at a 9–10 percent discount rate. AIXTRON ~~generated free cash flow in that band during the 2022–2023 peak, but materially below it in the softer 2024 environment~~==generated free cash flow of €7.7 million in FY2022, negative €109.7 million in FY2023, negative €72.4 million in FY2024, and positive €181.9 million in FY2025==. The market was therefore pricing in ~~either a prompt return to peak cash generation — plausible if the GaN power cycle accelerated through 2026–2028 — or a lower discount rate reflecting AIXTRON's net-cash balance sheet and the scarcity premium of being the only listed pure-play MOCVD specialist in Europe. Neither assumption is unreasonable; the uncertainty lies in timing rather than direction.~~==a cash-flow trajectory well above the FY2025 recovery year, supported by optoelectronics demand, later GaN normalisation, and the scarcity premium of being the only listed pure-play MOCVD specialist in Europe. The uncertainty lies in whether the required cash-flow step-up is a cycle peak or a durable new baseline.==

## Bull, Base, and Bear Scenarios

**Bull case — ~~€28–34~~==€53–56== per share.** ~~GaN power electronics adoption accelerates through the 2026–2028 automotive and data-centre power cycles; AIXTRON captures 60 percent-plus global market share in GaN MOCVD tooling; the SiC platform establishes durable revenue above €100 million annually; and micro-LED revives in some form — whether via Apple Watch successor, AR headsets, or industrial display applications — adding €50–80 million of incremental revenue.~~==Optoelectronics demand remains the main near-term volume driver; GaN power electronics accelerates through the 2027–2028 automotive and data-centre power cycles; AIXTRON sustains 60 percent-plus global market share in GaN MOCVD tooling; the SiC platform recovers as overcapacity clears; and micro-LED revives in some form — whether via Apple Watch successor, AR headsets, or industrial display applications — adding €50–80 million of incremental revenue.== Revenue reaches €900 million to €1 billion by fiscal 2027. EBIT margins re-expand to the 27–30 percent range on operating leverage. At a 28–30x forward P/E on normalised earnings of approximately €210 million, equity value approaches €6.0–6.3 billion — a stock price in the ~~high €20s to low €30s~~==low-to-mid €50s==. ~~This scenario requires the market to award the premium multiple it is currently withholding.~~==This scenario broadly matches the May 2026 snapshot price, so additional upside would require earnings above this path, a higher multiple, or favourable treatment of the convertible.==

**Base case — ~~€17–21~~==€30–34== per share.** ~~GaN power sustains a 15–18 percent revenue CAGR; SiC adds incremental but not transformative revenue; micro-LED remains dormant as a meaningful order contributor.~~==Optoelectronics carries the FY2026 recovery implied by the April guidance; GaN power grows steadily after a stable-to-moderate 2026; SiC remains incremental while overcapacity clears; micro-LED remains dormant as a meaningful order contributor.== Revenue grows to €720–780 million by 2027 at a 22–24 percent EBIT margin. Normalised earnings of roughly €130–145 million at a 22–24x forward P/E imply equity value of approximately €3.4–3.8 billion, a price of ~~€17–19~~==€30–34==. ~~This is the scenario closest to what consensus appeared to be discounting near the frozen date — modest re-rating but no heroics.~~==This scenario sits materially below the May 2026 snapshot price, which means the market was discounting more than a modest re-rating by the frozen date.==

**Bear case — ~~€8–11~~==€5–8== per share.** Chinese export-control tightening removes a significant customer cohort; GaN power adoption stalls as customers defer capacity amid macro uncertainty; SiC platform fails to win share against established suppliers; micro-LED never materialises. Revenue contracts toward €380–430 million with EBIT margins falling to the 10–13 percent range. At trough multiples of 14–16x forward earnings of approximately €45–55 million, equity value falls below €900 million — a stock price of ~~€8–10~~==€5–8==. This scenario is tail risk, but the LED MOCVD cycle demonstrated that AIXTRON can lose 70 percent of its revenue in a concentrated downturn when one application thesis collapses.

## The Consensus Gap

~~The central tension as of the frozen date was not about whether GaN power electronics was a real secular trend — that debate had largely been settled by cumulative industry data — but about the pace of the ramp, the duration of Chinese demand uncertainty, and whether AIXTRON would receive any valuation credit for the micro-LED option that had been so emphatically repriced out of the stock.~~==The central tension as of the frozen date was the durability of the optoelectronics-led demand inflection, the timing of any later GaN power acceleration, the duration of Chinese demand uncertainty, and whether AIXTRON would receive durable valuation credit for micro-LED optionality after the earlier repricing.== ~~Consensus appeared to be pricing a base-case trajectory without micro-LED recovery and with muted SiC contribution.~~==The May 2026 market price appeared to discount more than the base-case trajectory: SiC was still a slow-build, GaN was stable to moderately improving in the company's 2026 framework, and optoelectronics was carrying the near-term demand narrative.== ~~The dossier's read was modestly more constructive on GaN timing, more pessimistic on micro-LED in the near term, and aligned with consensus on SiC as a slow-build rather than an immediate catalyst.~~==The dossier's read is constructive only if the optoelectronics upswing proves durable and GaN power reaccelerates after 2026.== The gap between ~~€15 spot and the base-case €17–21 implied roughly 15–40 percent upside if the GaN power cycle delivered on its structural promise — a reasonable expected-value proposition for patient capital, but one that had said the same thing for the better part of two years without resolving~~==roughly €53.68 spot and the base-case €30–34 range leaves little margin for a merely normal cycle; upside requires the bull-case earnings path to arrive on schedule==.

chapters.title: Multi-year trajectory through GaN inflection, SiC ramp, and micro-LED reset
chapters.body:
## The Power Electronics Inflection: FY2022

AIXTRON arrived at fiscal 2022 carrying a compound-semiconductor order book reshaped by a decade of structural transition. The LED MOCVD wave that had powered the Herzogenrath company through the 2010s — and then punished it with brutal overcapacity — had largely passed. In its place, a quieter but more durable current had begun running through demand for gallium nitride: not the blue-LED chips that once lit smartphone screens, but power transistors switching electrical current in electric-vehicle onboard chargers, data-centre power supplies, and consumer fast chargers operating at voltages where GaN's switching speed and lower conduction losses outperformed silicon.

Full-year 2022 revenue reached approximately ~~€441 million~~ ==€463 million==, a meaningful step from prior years, as customers converted equipment reservations into purchase orders. Order intake ran ahead of revenue recognition, building a backlog that management described as giving the company "good visibility" into 2023. Felix Grawert, who had been repositioning AIXTRON's product roadmap since ~~taking the CEO role in 2018~~ ==joining the Executive Board in August 2017 and becoming CEO & President in March 2021==, described GaN power adoption on earnings calls as transitioning from an early-adopter technology to a "structural" demand driver — one that would persist across multiple customer-capital-expenditure cycles rather than collapsing into a single-wave event of the kind that had defined the LED era.

The geographic composition of that demand told a story about where the GaN power supply chain was consolidating most rapidly. Chinese power-device manufacturers, building out capacity to serve the domestic EV and fast-charging markets, accounted for a disproportionately large share of equipment orders. Renminbi translation into reporting euros added a layer of FX exposure that management flagged but characterised as manageable given the multi-year nature of equipment purchase decisions; order bookings in China were typically quoted in US dollars, partly insulating headline order intake from CNY moves while creating a second translation step when USD revenue was converted to EUR at recognition. This concentration would prove both an accelerant and, in later quarters, a source of volatility.

---

## ~~Record Revenue, Peaking Orders: FY2023~~ ==Step-Up Revenue, Rising Orders: FY2023==

Fiscal 2023 represented ~~the financial apex of~~ ==a major step-up in== AIXTRON's post-LED reconstruction. Revenue rose to approximately ~~€629 million~~ ==€629.9 million== as the company converted its strengthened backlog into shipped tools, and operating margins expanded to levels that reflected the leverage inherent in a capital-equipment franchise with high fixed-cost absorption. EBIT margins pushed into the ~~high-twenties percent range~~ ==mid-twenties percent range== — outperforming the guidance corridor management had issued at the start of the year, a pattern that had become familiar as GaN power demand ran hotter than mid-cycle estimates implied.

| Fiscal Year | Revenue (EUR, approx.) | YoY Change | EBIT Margin (approx.) |
|---|---|---|---|
| FY2021 | ~~€411M~~ ==€429M== | Recovery | ~~25%~~ ==23%== |
| FY2022 | ~~€441M~~ ==€463M== | ~~+7%~~ ==+8%== | ~~25%~~ ==23%== |
| FY2023 | ~~€629M~~ ==€630M== | ~~+43%~~ ==+36%== | ~~28–30%~~ ==25%== |
| FY2024 | ~~€600M+ range~~ ==€633M== | ~~Modest decline~~ ==Roughly flat/slightly up== | ~20–25% |

Yet even as revenue moved through its ~~record corridor~~ ==post-LED-cycle step-up==, order intake was already signalling a different trajectory. Customers who had placed reservations in 2021 and 2022 had received their tools and were now in the qualification-and-ramp phase, not the procurement phase. ~~Order intake declined from its 2022 peaks~~ ==Order intake rose to €640.7 million in FY2023, up 9% from €585.9 million in FY2022==, and Grawert framed this ~~normalisation~~ ==late-cycle digestion risk== in the second half of the year not as a demand problem but as an expected digestion period characteristic of the compound-semiconductor equipment cycle.

The micro-LED display thesis, which had animated analyst conversations since 2021, moved toward a more cautious register during 2023. Apple's reported plans to deploy micro-LED in the Apple Watch — a programme that would have required substantial AIXTRON MOCVD capacity for the III-nitride and III-phosphide compound structures involved — faced repeated internal reviews at the device company. Grawert maintained that the technology programme was architecturally intact but declined to attach revenue timelines to micro-LED equipment orders. The display application, he said on multiple occasions, remained a question of "when, not if," while acknowledging that capital-equipment revenue would lag any commercial product announcement by the typical fab-buildout cycle — eighteen months at minimum between tool order and volume-production yield.

---

## The SiC Adjacency

Running in parallel to the GaN power narrative, AIXTRON had been building a position in silicon carbide epitaxy. SiC CVD — chemical vapour deposition using a Planetary Reactor architecture that shares engineering heritage with the MOCVD platform — addresses the 650-volt-and-above power market where SiC's wider bandgap outperforms GaN. Electric-vehicle traction inverters, operating at voltages well above onboard charger topologies, represent the principal SiC application, and the automotive supply chain's commitment to SiC was translating into equipment demand for AIXTRON's G10-SiC reactor family.

The SiC business offered a counterweight to the China-heavy GaN order composition. European and North American automotive-supply-chain customers — building greenfield SiC fabs to serve committed EV platform programmes — were purchasing tools on capex cycles tied to OEM launch timelines rather than Chinese market dynamics. Reporting currency for European customers was typically euros, reducing FX translation friction relative to Asia-originated orders. Grawert described the SiC opportunity as "complementary" to GaN rather than substitutive: the two power-device technologies serving voltage tiers that did not compete directly, meaning AIXTRON could participate in both markets with a common platform philosophy, spreading R&D and service infrastructure across a broader installed base. He drew a consistent distinction between the EV megatrend as the structural macro driver and the specific compound-semiconductor technology choices — GaN or SiC — as the engineering decisions playing out inside that macro.

---

## Revenue Softening and Micro-LED Reset: FY2024

Fiscal 2024 confirmed the cyclical correction that order-intake trends had foreshadowed. Revenue ~~ran in the vicinity of the €600 million range, reflecting lower backlog conversion from a softer 2023 order intake~~ ==reached €633.2 million, roughly flat to slightly above FY2023 revenue of €629.9 million, while order intake softened as the prior power-electronics equipment cycle digested capacity additions==. The margin profile compressed from peak levels as fixed-cost absorption declined. AIXTRON's capital-light model — tool design and final assembly in Germany, components sourced globally — meant that the company maintained profitability through the trough, a structural advantage over the post-2012 LED collapse period when revenue fell by roughly two-thirds and operating losses accumulated for several years. The comparison underscored how substantially the business mix had improved: the power-electronics customer base carried longer replacement cycles and more durable qualification barriers than the commodity LED producers who had driven the earlier cycle.

The most significant narrative shift of 2024 was the effective reset of near-term micro-LED display expectations. Reports emerged that Apple had substantially deferred or internally shelved its micro-LED wearable programme in favour of continuing with OLED, removing what had been a speculative near-term catalyst from AIXTRON's demand model. The implied equipment procurement associated with that programme — potentially hundreds of millions of euros in tool orders across multiple vendors — would not materialise on the timelines the market had been pricing. Grawert addressed the development with characteristic precision on the Q4 2024 results call:

> "The micro-LED display timeline has extended. Our assessment of the long-term technology adoption has not changed, but we are not planning our 2025 or 2026 revenue around near-term display volume."

GaN power continued to generate recurring tool orders, but velocity had moderated from the Chinese-driven surge of 2022–2023. The deceleration partly reflected customer-fab utilisation: tools purchased at peak had not yet been fully loaded with production volume, reducing urgency for additional capacity additions. Dollar strength in parts of the year added a modest tailwind to USD-denominated order values when translated to euros for reported order intake, but provided limited buffer against the underlying volume decline. Grawert noted that GaN power adoption in non-Chinese markets — European automotive-adjacent applications and North American data-centre power conversion — was accelerating on a longer but more structurally stable adoption curve, providing a floor even as Chinese order cadence normalised.

---

## FY2025: ~~Recovery Trajectory~~ ==Contraction Year== and Structural Question

Entering fiscal 2025, AIXTRON management guided for ~~revenue recovery, underpinned by a SiC order pipeline that had strengthened as European automotive SiC fab programmes moved from planning into equipment procurement. The GaN power market was showing early signs of re-engagement from Chinese customers that had completed device qualifications and were extending capacity for the next wave of EV and fast-charging designs. Order intake began recovering, and management pointed to design-win momentum at power-IC customers across multiple geographies as a leading indicator of tool orders twelve to eighteen months forward~~ ==a softer market environment, and the year ultimately contracted: revenue declined 12% to €556.6 million and order intake declined 9% to €544.3 million. By the April 2026 update, management's FY2026 framework centred on optoelectronics as the main demand driver, with GaN stable to moderate and SiC weak amid overcapacity==.

The micro-LED thesis remained live but distant. The earliest plausible commercial re-entry point for a large-programme tool order had shifted to the latter half of the decade, making display-related equipment revenue a 2027–2028 event at best rather than a near-term catalyst. Grawert maintained that AIXTRON's MOCVD platform held incumbent technology status for whatever micro-LED production ramp eventually arrived, and that ongoing development-tool shipments to display-research customers were preserving both process knowledge and customer relationships through the delay.

For the multi-year earnings story, the structural question had clarified into a single frame: could ~~the SiC ramp grow fast enough — and the GaN power cycle recover durably enough — to more than offset the residual LED MOCVD revenue decline and the deferred micro-LED upside~~ ==optoelectronics demand scale fast enough — while GaN power remained stable and SiC worked through overcapacity — to offset the deferred micro-LED upside and the residual cyclicality of compound-semiconductor tool demand==, while sustaining the margin profile that had made AIXTRON's reconstituted compound-semiconductor franchise so much more attractive than its LED-era predecessor. By the close of the frozen-window period, the G5 and G10 Planetary Reactor families were the incumbent tools of record for the two largest next-generation power markets in the global electrification build-out. Whether that incumbency was monetised in a tight two-year window or a stretched four-year cycle remained, as it has throughout AIXTRON's history, the irreducible variable in the investment case.

chapters.title: Felix Grawert, Christian Danninger, Executive Board, Supervisory Board
chapters.body:
The company that became AIXTRON was built inside a university. In December 1983, three researchers at RWTH Aachen's Institute for Semiconductor Technology — Dr. Holger Jürgensen, Dr. Meino Heyen, and Heinrich Schumann — incorporated a spin-out whose very name encoded its origins: "Aix-la-Chapelle," the ancient French designation for Aachen, fused with "electronics." Jürgensen's founding maxim was blunt: "The future belongs to optoelectronics." The first MOCVD system the company commissioned arrived in 1985, built for a market that, as Heyen later recalled, did not yet exist in commercial form. That disposition — designing tools for adoption curves not yet visible to the buyer — would define the firm's institutional character across the decades that followed, and it shaped the type of manager who eventually rose to lead it.

## Felix Grawert: An Engineer Trained on Three Continents

Felix Grawert arrived at AIXTRON in August 2017 from a career that had moved through academia, strategy consulting, and industrial product management in an arc that was unusual for a German Mittelstand equipment company. Born in Kiel in 1975, he earned a Diplom-Ingenieur in electrical engineering from the Universität Karlsruhe before crossing the Atlantic: a Master of Science from Georgia Tech, followed by a doctorate in electrical engineering and computer science from the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, completed in 2005. The MIT PhD was not honorary ballast — it centred on power conversion and semiconductor device physics, the technical substrate on which AIXTRON's GaN and SiC equipment ambitions would later rest.

From 2005 to 2013, Grawert worked as a consultant at McKinsey & Company in Munich, eventually reaching Associate Principal. His sector focus was semiconductors, high technology, and automotive — a triangulation that would prove directly applicable when GaN-on-silicon power electronics began displacing silicon MOSFETs in automotive on-board chargers and data-centre power conversion. He left McKinsey in 2013 for Infineon Technologies, where he served until 2017 as Head of Product Line High Voltage Conversion in Munich and Villach, overseeing the commercial execution of exactly the device category that AIXTRON's G10-GaN platform was designed to enable. When the AIXTRON Supervisory Board went looking for a board-level candidate who combined deep technical grounding in power semiconductors with commercial and strategic discipline, Grawert was an identifiable profile.

He joined the Executive Board in August 2017 alongside co-President Bernd Schulte. For the first three and a half years, the two men ran the company as a diarchy — Grawert taking responsibility for sales, marketing, customer relations, and R&D, Schulte managing operations and manufacturing. [AIXTRON IR](https://www.aixtron.com/en/company/management/executive-board)

## The Schulte Transition and the End of a Multi-Decade Tenure

Bernd Schulte's retirement in March 2021 closed one of the longer continuous tenures in AIXTRON's leadership history. He had joined the company in 1993, when the LED MOCVD market was still embryonic, and assumed a seat on the Executive Board in 2002. Over nineteen years as a board member — the majority of AIXTRON's existence as a listed company — Schulte had navigated the LED equipment cycle's 2007–2011 boom, the sharp post-boom correction as Chinese capacity flooded the market, and the years of restructuring and diversification that followed. He had been present when the company pivoted from LED-dominated revenues toward the power-electronics and photonics mix that now characterises the order book.

His departure at the expiry of his contract on 31 March 2021 was orderly rather than abrupt — the Supervisory Board had announced the succession mechanics in May 2020, giving the market twelve months of advance notice. Grawert assumed the sole chairmanship of the Executive Board on 1 April 2021. The Supervisory Board simultaneously announced that the board would be expanded by the addition of a dedicated CFO position and a new COO.

## Christian Danninger: The Austrian CFO

Dr. Christian Danninger joined as Chief Financial Officer and Executive Board member in May 2021, filling the finance seat that had not previously existed as a standalone Vorstand position. Born in 1979 in Gmunden, Austria, Danninger brought an unusual credential set for a semiconductor equipment company: a doctorate in law from Johannes Kepler University in Linz, supplemented by dual master's degrees in law and business administration. His career had been built in industrial capital-equipment businesses — fifteen years between 2005 and 2021 split across the ENGEL Group, the Austrian plastics-injection-machinery maker, and PUTZMEISTER Holding, the German concrete-pump manufacturer where he had served as CFO from 2017. The profile — a trained lawyer-turned-capital-equipment CFO, comfortable with export-heavy manufacturing businesses and complex international customer financing — suited AIXTRON's profile as a EUR-reporting company selling long-cycle capital equipment globally. Danninger's contract runs to April 2029. [AIXTRON IR](https://www.aixtron.com/en/company/management/executive-board)

## The Linck Interlude and a Lean Two-Person Board

The third Executive Board member appointed in 2021, Dr. Jochen Linck, served as Chief Operating Officer with responsibility for R&D and operations — procurement, manufacturing, logistics, quality, and IT. Linck's departure in September 2023, which the company disclosed in May of that year as a decision not to renew his contract for personal reasons, reduced the Vorstand back to two members. Rather than appointing a successor to the COO seat, AIXTRON created an internal Executive Committee — a layer of senior vice presidents covering the former COO portfolio — that reports directly to Grawert and Danninger. The structure has been characterised internally as a deliberate move toward operating flexibility, concentrating formal accountability at the top while distributing functional depth below board level. [AIXTRON press release, May 2023](https://www.aixtron.com/en/press/press-releases/AIXTRON%20introduces%20new%20Executive%20Committee%20/%20Current%20COO%20Jochen%20Linck%20not%20to%20renew%20his%20contract%20due%20to%20personal%20reasons%20/%20New%20Executive%20Committee%20will%20support%20CEO%20and%20CFO_n2443)

The Supervisory Board's decision in September 2024 to extend Grawert's contract by a further five years — through 13 August 2030 — reflected a verdict on the first three years of his sole tenure. Then-chairman Kim Schindelhauer described the extension in explicit strategic terms: "With Dr Grawert, Aixtron made significant progress in the equipment technology for power electronics." Grawert, in his own statement, kept the language operational: "I am very excited to continue my work at Aixtron and further shape the future." [Compound Semiconductor, September 2024](https://compoundsemiconductor.net/article/120135/Aixtron_extends_CEOand_s_contract)

## Grawert's Strategic Voice

On earnings calls, Grawert tends toward declarative technical-commercial framing rather than promotional tone. The vocabulary of the GaN power thesis — 800-volt architectures, data-centre power-conversion density, the timing of automotive adoption curves — is handled with the precision of someone who ran a power-semiconductor product line, not a generalist CEO who acquired the terminology from investor-relations briefing books. Presenting full-year 2025 results in early 2026 — a year in which revenue fell 12 percent year-on-year to €556.6m and EBIT compressed to €100.3m — he did not attempt to obscure the cyclical softness, but framed the forward thesis clearly:

> "In 2026, optical data communication for AI applications and GaN power will be the main source of revenue. We expect that AI data centers can become the largest single application for GaN power semiconductors in the near future."
