The ~~implied FY2026-to-FY2027 EPS growth of 20–25% is the number that justifies the current valuation — a P/E in the high-teens to low-twenties on a forward basis — and is entirely contingent on the order intake recovery manifesting in H2 2026 shipments~~ ==valuation case at the May 22, 2026 trading price of about €53.68 rests on whether FY2027 can show enough revenue and margin acceleration to make the premium multiple credible; it is contingent on order intake improving in H2 2026 and converting into 2027 shipments==.

## Management guidance

AIXTRON ~~issued its initial FY2026 guidance alongside the FY2025 full-year results in early 2026~~ ==had updated its FY2026 framework by April 2026, after preliminary Q1 figures, to revenue around €560m in a range of plus/minus €30m and an EBIT margin around 17–20%==. The company's guidance format is a revenue range plus an EBIT margin corridor, ~~without quarterly breakdown~~ ==with Q2 2026 revenue guided around €110m plus/minus €10m but no full quarterly bridge==. At the time of the frozen snapshot, ~~Grawert's communicated framework for 2026 pointed toward a revenue recovery year, with the GaN power recovery and SiC ramp cited as the primary volume drivers~~ ==AIXTRON's communicated framework was optoelectronics-led, with GaN stable to moderate and SiC weak because of overcapacity==.

~~From the FY2025 earnings call, Grawert framed the demand environment in characteristically direct terms:~~

> ~~"We see the GaN power market returning to a healthy order intake level. The inventory digestion at our customers is largely complete, and we are seeing renewed conversations about capacity additions — particularly in Asia, but also in Europe with our strategic accounts."~~

==The practical read-through for the next 12 months is therefore less a broad power-electronics rebound than a test of whether optoelectronics strength can bridge a slower GaN/SiC recovery.==

~~On the SiC opportunity, the message has been more measured:~~

> ~~"SiC power epitaxy is a growing part of our business. We are competing hard, and we are winning. The qualification timelines are longer than GaN, but once a customer qualifies our G10-SiC platform, the relationship is sticky."~~

==The guidance framework should be verified against AIXTRON's published quarterly disclosures at [investors.aixtron.com](https://investors.aixtron.com).==

~~Both statements, sourced from AIXTRON's investor relations record, should be verified against the full FY2025 transcript at [investors.aixtron.com](https://investors.aixtron.com).~~

## Metrics to watch each quarter

Not all data points in AIXTRON's quarterly releases carry equal weight. Four numbers govern the thesis:

**Order intake** is the primary leading indicator, disclosed quarterly. A sustainable ~~recovery~~ ==FY2027 growth case== requires consecutive quarters above €150m — below that level, the revenue recovery stalls in two to three quarters. Order intake below €130m for any quarter in H2 2026 would be a material miss.

**Equipment revenue mix by platform** — the split between GaN power, SiC power, photonics/optoelectronics, and micro-LED — tells the quality of ~~the recovery~~ ==the FY2026 guide and FY2027 setup==. A revenue recovery ~~led entirely by photonics (laser diodes, VCSELs for datacom) is lower-quality than one anchored in GaN and SiC power, which carry higher average selling prices and longer installed-base aftermarket tails~~ ==led by optoelectronics would be consistent with AIXTRON's April 2026 demand framing; the higher-quality upside case would be optoelectronics strength plus visible stabilization in GaN and evidence that SiC overcapacity is easing==.

**China revenue share** has historically represented 40–55% of total. A return to that share range would confirm Chinese device-maker investment resumption; a sustained decline below 35% would signal either export-control friction or a structural loss of share to domestic Chinese MOCVD equipment providers.

**Gross margin** — AIXTRON ~~does not break this out separately but it can be inferred from the revenue and EBIT figures~~ ==discloses gross profit and gross margin directly; FY2025 gross margin was 40% and Q1 2026 gross margin was 18%==. A ~~recovering gross margin (toward 45–48%) would confirm the product mix is shifting toward higher-value GaN and SiC tools from lower-margin spares and service work. A flat or falling gross margin alongside growing revenue would signal margin dilution from aggressive pricing in a contested competitive environment~~ ==recovery from the Q1 trough toward the FY2025 level would confirm volume and mix normalization, while a flat or falling disclosed gross margin alongside growing revenue would signal margin dilution from aggressive pricing in a contested competitive environment==.

## Beat versus miss

A beat in any given quarter requires three things to come together: order intake above the high end of consensus (call it €155–160m for Q2 2026), revenue at or above the upper half of ~~the guidance range~~ ==AIXTRON's Q2 revenue guide of around €110m plus/minus €10m==, and a commentary from Grawert indicating that the order book for H2 2026 tool deliveries is firm. An earnings beat that is accompanied by guidance held flat or trimmed would be market-neutral at best.

A miss has a specific texture at AIXTRON: it is almost always order-intake-led rather than revenue-led, because the backlog provides a quarter or two of buffer. If order intake falls materially short — below €120m in any individual quarter — the market will extrapolate that into a revenue hole in 2027, regardless of what Q2 2026 sales actually print. The asymmetry of the earnings read is therefore heavily front-loaded toward the order intake line, not the P&L.

## The asymmetry: bull and bear

The bull setup into May 2027 is coherent and supported by structural demand. ~~GaN power electronics for data centre server boards, EV on-board chargers, and industrial motor drives represents a multi-year tool procurement cycle that is only in its second or third inning globally~~ ==Near term, optoelectronics is the clearest demand support, while GaN power electronics for data centre server boards, EV on-board chargers, and industrial motor drives remains the structural swing factor for a multi-year tool procurement cycle==. If ~~Infineon's Kulim GaN fab in Malaysia~~ ==Infineon's 200 mm SiC power fab in Kulim, Malaysia, whose first phase includes GaN epitaxy,== and the European GaN capacity additions at STMicro proceed as announced, AIXTRON captures a substantial share of that capex. Add a recovery in China orders (50% of historical revenue, depressed through 2024–2025), a credible SiC foothold, and the possibility that a renewed micro-LED programme — whether from a display maker in South Korea or a US hyperscaler — emerges as a 2027–2028 catalyst. In that scenario, FY2027 revenue of €720–740m with a 25–26% EBIT margin is ~~not an aggressive forecast; it implies a stock with meaningful upside from the current trading range~~ ==the high end of the bull case rather than the base case; at the May 22, 2026 trading price of about €53.68, it would still need to support a premium multiple rather than merely close a valuation discount==.

The bear setup is specific. AIXTRON's China exposure has become a geopolitical variable: MOCVD equipment for power electronics has not yet been subject to the same export-control scrutiny as leading-edge logic tools, but any extension of restrictions to compound-semiconductor equipment would cut the addressable market materially and abruptly. Separately, the GaN power recovery thesis could again prove premature — Chinese device makers added capacity so aggressively in 2022–2023 that a second digestion phase, triggered by slower-than-expected EV adoption or a data-centre capex pause, is not impossible. And the SiC competitive position remains genuinely contested: Veeco, Nuflare, and emerging domestic Chinese suppliers are all targeting the same spec sheets. A scenario in which AIXTRON ~~recovers to only €580–600m in FY2026~~ ==lands around the lower half of its €530–590m FY2026 revenue guide== and guides FY2027 flat implies a P/E re-rating that would be painful from current levels.

The asymmetry, as it stands at the frozen snapshot, ~~tilts modestly toward the bull~~ ==is balanced rather than clearly bullish at the €53.68 snapshot price==. The ~~order intake data through Q1 2026 has shown tentative improvement; the SiC programme is generating first revenue; and the China business, while uncertain, has stabilised rather than deteriorated further~~ ==April 2026 guide raised FY2026 revenue to around €560m plus/minus €30m, but the demand mix was optoelectronics-led, GaN was stable to moderate, and SiC remained weak because of overcapacity==. The next four quarters will not resolve all of this — but by March 2027, when ~~Grawert publishes~~ ==AIXTRON publishes== the FY2026 actuals and the FY2027 outlook, the compound-semi capital cycle will have revealed enough of its shape to make the valuation case either compelling or uncomfortable.

chapters.title: GaN power scaling, SiC ramp, photonics demand, 2026-2030 horizon
chapters.body:
## The G10 at Scale: GaN Power's Inflection Curve

By spring 2026, AIXTRON's G10-GaN platform had moved past proof-of-concept and into what Grawert described as the installed-base accumulation phase of GaN power electronics adoption. The transition was structural rather than cyclical in character: gallium-nitride power semiconductors were displacing silicon MOSFET and IGBT designs across a widening application set — electric-vehicle onboard chargers, server power-supply units serving hyperscale data centres, and consumer fast-charging adapters that had become standard-issue for premium mobile hardware. Each design win at a volume device manufacturer translated, on a multi-year lag, into capital-equipment orders as fabs committed to production-scale capacity.

The competitive alignment that AIXTRON had built through its proprietary ~~close-coupled showerhead reactor architecture~~ ==Planetary Reactor technology== remained the principal moat. GaN-on-Si epitaxy demanded tight uniformity control across 200mm and larger-diameter wafers; the G10's process architecture addressed that requirement in a way that rival MOCVD suppliers had struggled to replicate at production yield and cost. Customers including [Infineon Technologies](https://www.infineon.com), [STMicroelectronics](https://www.st.com), Navitas Semiconductor, and a growing cohort of Chinese domestic GaN-on-Si manufacturers all relied on AIXTRON toolsets to varying degrees, giving Herzogenrath a cross-geography footprint that no single competitor matched.

Yet the GaN adoption curve remained sensitive to end-market timing. The push toward 800-volt EV architectures had accelerated GaN displacement of silicon in automotive power conversion, but the broader consumer and industrial refresh cycle was uneven across regions. Order intake data — the leading indicator for AIXTRON's revenue on a typical six-to-twelve-month conversion lag — suggested that European and North American automotive-driven demand was consolidating into steady-state replenishment, while Chinese domestic GaN fabs were adding capacity at a pace informed as much by industrial policy as by near-term device demand. The latter created both an opportunity and a concentration risk that Grawert had flagged in investor communications as requiring monitoring.

## SiC: The Second Front

AIXTRON's entry into silicon carbide power epitaxy represented a deliberate strategic broadening, and by early 2026 it had become the company's most closely watched forward variable. The SiC power device market had long been served by specialised chemical-vapour-deposition reactor suppliers — including Wolfspeed's captive epi capacity and a handful of Asian specialists — designed from the outset for the higher process temperatures and corrosive chemistries that SiC deposition demanded. AIXTRON's arrival with the G10-SiC platform introduced a new variable into that competitive structure.

The commercial case rested on process flexibility and customer-base overlap. For device manufacturers running mixed compound-semiconductor roadmaps — GaN at lower voltages, SiC across the 650V-to-1700V range where silicon carbide held the switching efficiency advantage — sourcing epitaxy equipment from a single vendor carried procurement and process-knowledge advantages. AIXTRON's existing G10 service infrastructure, spares network, and applications engineering relationships provided a differentiated entry path relative to a greenfield competitor.

Wolfspeed's well-publicised capital-intensity challenges and the broader SiC supply-chain recalibration following the 2021–2023 investment surge had created an ambiguous demand backdrop. Several SiC device makers trimmed near-term expansion plans as EV ramp timelines slipped from original projections, creating a measured rather than urgent appetite for new epi capacity. Grawert framed the SiC opportunity as a multi-year ramp in line with a product line still building its reference-customer list — a disciplined positioning that avoided over-promising against a qualification cycle that, by the nature of SiC process validation, stretched twelve to eighteen months between initial assessment and volume order placement.

## Photonics: The Quiet Growth Vector

The photonics franchise — laser diodes for datacom transceivers, VCSELs for three-dimensional sensing, and InP-based components for automotive LiDAR — attracted less investor attention than the power-electronics narrative, but by 2026 it had emerged as a more consistent and less cyclical revenue contributor than the GaN and SiC headlines implied.

The AI infrastructure build-out had become the principal near-term demand driver. 800G and emerging 1.6T optical transceivers connecting GPU clusters inside hyperscale data centres required high volumes of GaAs and InP laser diodes, and AIXTRON's ~~G5 and G10 optoelectronic reactor platforms~~ ==G10-AsP Planetary Reactor-based optoelectronics platform, alongside legacy optoelectronic toolsets,== sat in the epitaxy step for that supply chain. Customers including [Coherent](https://www.coherent.com) (the combined II-VI and Finisaw entity), Lumentum, and a constellation of Asian laser-diode manufacturers had sustained tool demand through the period as transceiver makers added wafer-start capacity to serve accelerating GPU interconnect requirements.

Automotive LiDAR provided a second growth vector with a distinct demand cycle. The shift from mechanical spinning units to solid-state LiDAR architectures increased laser-diode content per vehicle, and AIXTRON's InP and GaAs reactor platforms were embedded in the supply chains of several ADAS-component manufacturers preparing for higher-volume deployments. Though LiDAR volumes remained modest relative to AI datacom as of the snapshot date, the application provided diversification against hyperscaler capital-expenditure cycles — a property that Grawert had highlighted as the photonics mix became more strategically significant within the company's overall revenue composition.

| Segment | Substrate | Tool platform | Principal demand driver (2026) |
|---|---|---|---|
| GaN power electronics | GaN-on-Si, GaN-on-SiC | G10-GaN | EV onboard chargers, data-centre PSU |
| SiC power devices | 4H-SiC | G10-SiC | EV traction inverters, industrial drives |
| Datacom laser diodes | GaAs, InP | ~~G5/G10 optoelectronics~~ ==G10-AsP and legacy optoelectronics== | AI cluster interconnect, 800G/1.6T |
| Automotive LiDAR | GaAs, InP | ~~G5/G10 optoelectronics~~ ==G10-AsP and legacy optoelectronics== | ADAS Level 3+ solid-state sensors |
| VCSEL / 3D sensing | GaAs | G5 | Consumer depth sensing |
| Micro-LED display | InGaN / GaN-on-sapphire | Specialised platform | Speculative; programme delays |

## The Micro-LED Residual Option

The micro-LED display thesis had been the most visible source of AIXTRON narrative risk since early 2024, when press reports indicated that Apple had postponed or cancelled its planned micro-LED Apple Watch display programme. The reports were never officially confirmed by Apple, but they reset expectations across the equipment supply chain for the magnitude and timing of capacity orders. AIXTRON had developed specialised reactor capabilities for micro-LED epitaxy — the process of growing red, green, and blue LED pixels small enough for direct-view display applications at pixel pitches below fifty micrometres. The technical challenge was formidable: micro-LED manufacturing required epitaxial uniformity and defect-density control an order of magnitude tighter than standard LED production, and no display-scale manufacturing line had achieved the yield required for consumer-price-point products as of the frozen snapshot.

Management had consistently positioned the opportunity as an option rather than a plan, avoiding the trap of embedding speculative display demand into financial guidance. That discipline served the company's credibility through the 2024 disappointment. The option value remained asymmetric: if a major consumer OEM restarted a micro-LED programme and reached manufacturing readiness by 2027 or 2028, the resulting capacity build-out would represent a step-change in AIXTRON's addressable market — potentially several hundred million euros in incremental tool revenue across a two-to-three-year window. If the technology stalled, as OLED continued to advance its own brightness and efficiency roadmap, micro-LED would contribute near zero to the 2026–2030 revenue trajectory.

## The 2026–2030 Horizon

Standing at the frozen snapshot date, AIXTRON's strategic posture was defined by three structural convictions and one open question. The convictions: that GaN power electronics would continue migrating from design-win phase into volume production, sustaining multi-year installed-base expansion for the G10-GaN platform; that ~~SiC would graduate from qualification-phase revenue into a commercially material product line, with timing contingent on the customer qualification outcomes seeded in 2024 and 2025~~ ==SiC remained a multi-year product-line opportunity but faced a weak near-term demand backdrop as overcapacity weighed on customer expansion plans==; and that photonics demand — anchored by the AI data-centre interconnect build — would provide a revenue floor through any near-term power-electronics inventory correction.

The open question remained micro-LED. AIXTRON's guidance frameworks, as communicated through [investors.aixtron.com](https://investors.aixtron.com), did not explicitly embed large-scale display orders into base-case scenarios. That conservatism was appropriate given the programme-cancellation backdrop, and it meant that any re-emergence of a display-scale micro-LED procurement would represent upside to consensus rather than a make-or-break variable.

The capital cycle governing all of this was ultimately a function of device manufacturers' willingness to commit fab expansion capex — and AIXTRON, as a tool supplier rather than a chip producer, had no direct exposure to semiconductor end demand. That positioning was the source of both its leverage and its characteristic cyclicality. When GaN and SiC device fabs expanded capacity, AIXTRON's order intake moved first; when fabs paused to digest installed capacity, revenue compressed. The structural argument for the 2026–2030 period was that the demand base had become meaningfully more distributed than the LED MOCVD era had delivered: multiple end markets, multiple geographies, multiple substrate technologies operating on partially uncorrelated investment timelines. Whether that diversification would produce a smoother capital cycle or merely a more complex one remained, as of the snapshot, the central empirical question for the years ahead.
